 ‘Daddy Dale’: Shaquille O’Neal, former players deliver emotional tribute to LSU legend Dale Brown 
 Shaquille O’Neal reflected on the lasting impact of his former coach as loved ones gathered to celebrate the life of former LSU men’s basketball coach Dale Brow By Perry Robinson Published : Nov. 12, 2026 at 6:32 AM CST | Updated : 16 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BATON ROUGE, La. (WAFB) - Shaquille O’Neal reflected on the lasting impact of his former coach and a regret he wishes he could change as family, friends and former players gathered to celebrate the life of former LSU men’s basketball coach Dale Brown.
 O’Neal, who played for Brown at LSU before going on to become one of the NBA’s biggest stars, shared an emotional message during Brown’s celebration of life inside the Pete Maravich Assembly Center.
 “I’ve won on every level except college. My only regret is that I wasn’t good enough to win a national championship here,” O’Neal said.
 But his biggest regret went beyond basketball.
 O’Neal said he never got the chance to tell Brown he loved him one last time. He reflected on losing his sister and former NBA teammate Kobe Bryant, saying he wished he had expressed those feelings before they died.
 “My sister passed away and I didn’t get a chance to tell her I love her. Kobe Bryant died and I forgot to tell him I love him. Now my ‘Daddy Dale’ is gone, and I forgot to tell him I love him,” O’Neal said.
 He closed his remarks by thanking those in attendance and expressing his love for everyone gathered to remember Brown.
 Brown died in October at 90. During his time leading the LSU men’s basketball program, he won more than 400 games and helped establish the Tigers as a national basketball powerhouse.
 The celebration of life brought together those who knew Brown best to remember his impact both on and off the basketball court.
 “He was a real change agent. Never give up, keep moving forward, take the good with the bad and make it work,” former LSU player Collis Temple, Jr. said.
 Others remembered Brown as someone who inspired people to persevere and make a difference.
 “If we can be half the humanitarian he was, this would be a great place,” former LSU player Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf said.
